Dangerous humid heat through the day

Bars: number of 0.5° cells (about 50 km) at wet-bulb ≥ 28 °C. Click a bar to jump to that hour.

Why wet-bulb? It is the lowest temperature sweat can cool you to. Dry heat in the desert can top 44 °C with a wet-bulb near 21 °C; the Gulf Coast at 33 °C can be far more dangerous. That is the difference between the two views.
Source: Google Maps Platform weather insights (testing program), BigQuery view weather_history_us, queried 2026-10-20. Native grid ~4.6 km, averaged here to 0.5° cells (max for wet-bulb and heat index). State lines: US Census via us-atlas.
